prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: authorized, traceable hospital dispensing/returns. Aliases/producers: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway—Order Reconciliation Snapshot; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot—Priority Refill Tote Tag; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station—Batch Release Note; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk—Return Bin; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician—Cold Chain Handoff Card; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Producers: Clinical Pharmacist—Dose Exception Review Slip; Hospital Courier—Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; East Tube Dispatch Console—Tube Route Exception Ticket; Charge Nurse—Cabinet Downtime Notice; Medication Safety Officer—Diversion Review Packet. Morrowglass validates orders, holds unresolved/canceled/duplicate/superseded orders, rejects invalid updates with reasons. Cinderwake consumes Snapshot, reconciles orders/dispenses/balances using stable identifiers; preserves context/timestamps, verifies authorization, excludes cancellations, replaces supersessions, flags duplicates, subtracts partial dispenses conservatively; discrepancies hold with audit. Release requires order/instruction/product/destination agreement and identifiers/time/credentials. Copperfield requires reconciliation; checks packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain, reverifies delays; no dose decisions. Juniper blocks discrepancies; exceptions require evidence/authorized disposition. Clinical Pharmacist reviews concerns; inconclusive cases remain held; corrections require authorized orders. Larkspur locks transactions/confirms nonadministration; no bypass/substitution. Serious exceptions escalate immediately. Medication Safety Officer reviews harm/diversion; IT Operations Specialist receives Packet, examines logs without clinical changes; Stonewake assesses faults/restoration. Dispositions record reviewer/evidence/outcome. Courier collects closed ready-recorded bins; reconcile manifests before Pneumatic Tube Network admission; East checks routes; West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing. North Ward Cabinet Controller applies ward location/product/threshold/role/transaction-limit configuration; inventory=count+movements; thresholds never override clinical restrictions. Authenticate appropriate roles; high-risk removals may require confirmation; reject identity/location mismatch. Changes require version/review/effective-time/approver; absent current approval blocks routine dispensing/reports investigation. Bluejay logs compartment temperatures/probe identities/calibration, timed readings, approved limits, medication/lot/expiry, access identity/time/stock, door duration. Excursions/unavailable probes alarm/hold stock controlled; compare handoff custody-time/history. Clinical Pharmacist decides release/quarantine/discard; lot disposition prevents

New part:
S183: East Tube Dispatch Console maintains the approved route map and the current availability status of supported pneumatic segments.
S184: East Tube Dispatch Console checks the selected route against the destination cabinet, current network availability, and approved routing configuration before releasing a capsule.
S185: The console confirms that the destination is reachable and that the route does not include a segment reported unavailable.
S186: Route selection uses the destination identifier and the latest approved configuration version rather than an operator-entered sequence of segments.
S187: Before dispatch, the console checks for conflicting capsule movements and confirms that required interlocks are satisfied.
S188: The Pneumatic Tube Network reports segment status, transfer progress, and delivery confirmation to the dispatch console.
S189: If route status is stale or incomplete, the console holds the capsule and displays the condition for operator review.
S190: A loss of communication with a route sensor prevents the console from treating the affected segment as available.
S191: An interruption during transit is recorded with the capsule identifier, last confirmed location, and time of the interruption.
S192: The console alerts a Pharmacy Technician when a transfer stops progressing or cannot be confirmed at its destination.
S193: After recovery, the console requires refreshed segment status and an approved route decision before dispatch resumes.
S194: Route and temperature records retain timestamps and equipment identifiers to support operational review and investigation.
S195: The Pharmacy Verification Station serves as the final controlled checkpoint before a medication is made available for dispensing.
S196: The Clinical Pharmacist compares the active medication order with the product, strength, dosage form, dose, route, and scheduled time.
S197: The Clinical Pharmacist also confirms that the patient identifiers and pharmacy label agree with the authorized order.
S198: The Pharmacy Technician checks package integrity, lot identification, and expiry before presenting the medication for verification.
S199: For designated high-risk medications, an independent second check is completed and recorded before authorization.
S200: Any mismatch places the medication on hold until the discrepancy is resolved by an authorized pharmacy professional.
S201: The verification record captures the approving staff identity, time, and medication identifiers for later review.
S202: The Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot remains inhibited from completing a dispense until the required pharmacy authorization is present.
S203: The Clinical Pharmacist resolves unclear or conflicting order details through the Medication Order Gateway before authorizing release.
S204: The South Ward Cabinet Controller receives the release note and applies its own approved cabinet configuration before enabling any compartment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
